title: Forex reserves decline by $14 billion to $705 billion amid valuation effects, gold price decline - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
After touching a peak of $785.706 billion in the week ended September 4, 2026, forex reserves have been on a sustained decline | Photo Credit: Dado Ruvic

India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by a whopping $14.205 billion in the week ended November 13, 2026, to stand at $705.342 billion, a level last seen in the July-end/early August 2026 period.

The drop in the reserves came even as the rupee cumulatively appreciated 62 paise during the week, supported by FPI inflows aggregating $4.826 billion, into the equity markets, to close at 93.91 per US dollar on November 13, 2026.

Madan Sabnavis, Chief Economist, Bank of Baroda, said: “The fall in forex reserves could mainly be due to valuation reasons -- as the dollar is getting stronger, reserves are getting valued lower. Moreover, the price of gold, an important component of the reserves, has also come down. And there could also be dollar sales by RBI.”

After touching a peak of $785.706 billion in the week ended September 04, 2026, the reserves have been falling continuously.

In the reporting week, the drop in reserves was primarily due to the foreign currency assets and gold reserves declining by $7.897 billion and $6.183 billion, respectively. The other two components of the reserves too dipped -- special drawing rights (by $92 million) and reserve position in the IMF (32 million).
